keyFindings.description: #2480 is CONFLICTING (mergeStateStatus DIRTY) at fb584253, so GitHub runs no pull-request checks: no code head of this PR has finished CI. git merge-tree with main a1a134a3 conflicts only in packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch/README.md. Forward-merge main (never rebase), resolve the README row, push without a skip-checks trailer, and then CI runs at the merged head.

mutation.go:478 re-anchors at the quote's nearest occurrence, even one where the mark is not allowed. So an upload that only adds a copy of anchored text (a front-matter title equal to a commented heading, or a code block quoting an ask's text above it) is refused 400 'would land in the front matter / a code block; move that text out of it', though the anchored text is untouched. The deep review reproduced both cases with go test -overlay. On the base this was a 500; the PR now presents it as the caller's error, with advice that drops the user's new text. Fix: on a MarkNotAllowedError, re-anchor at the nearest occurrence where the mark is allowed, and refuse only when none is; add a test.

The 500 fallback at mutation.go:487-490 has no test. The deep review replaced it with `return refusedReanchor(...)`, which drops a refusal silently and writes the room without the anchor, and every docs test still passed. Make the decision one function that returns ErrInvalidMarkdown or a plain ErrDocSchema (not documentSchemaError, whose OutsideSchemaError means a stored tree to repair), and test both outcomes.

The place name is chosen in two packages: Place() returns 'the front matter' or the raw 'code_block', and mutation.go:540 swaps 'code_block' for 'a code block'. Let Place() return the reader's wording for both, and update reanchor_test.go:479.

accepted: Round-2 findings fixed in bf2118ca and confirmed by the tester on a real server: the sentinel/typed error marks only the mark-not-allowed refusal, every other error stays 500, the front matter is named, and the dead fallback is gone. Not a defect: ErrMarkNotAllowed and *MarkNotAllowedError are two names for one refusal (both documented, both tested).
